title: Roman-Style Sheet-Pan Pizza with Tomato-Mozzarella and Rosemary-Potato Halves
summary: A light, airy, crisp-based tray pizza made from a cold-fermented dough, topped half with tomato, mozzarella and basil and half with thin rosemary potatoes and Parmesan. Cut into rectangles for a crowd.
equipment: 30 x 40 cm rimmed metal baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
can whole peeled plum tomatoes (no added salt)
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh mozzarella (1 ball), torn and patted dry
waxy potatoes, sliced 2 mm thick (a mandoline helps)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix the wet dough
steps.text: The day before, stir the flour and yeast together, add the water and 2 tbsp dough oil and mix with a spatula to a shaggy, sticky dough. Rest for 10 minutes, sprinkle over the salt and squeeze it in with wet hands, then rest for 20 minutes. The high water content is what gives the finished crust its open, airy holes.

steps.title: Fold for strength
steps.text: With wet hands, lift one edge of the dough and fold it to the middle, turning the bowl a quarter and repeating 6 times. Rest for 20 minutes and repeat the folds twice more, 20 minutes apart, until the dough feels smoother and holds its shape. Folding builds strength in this very wet dough without kneading; cover and refrigerate for 16-24 hours.

steps.title: Press into the tray
steps.text: Oil the tray with 2 tbsp of the tray oil, tip the cold dough onto it and press it out gently with oiled fingertips; it will not reach the corners yet. Cover loosely and leave at room temperature for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, pressing it towards the corners after the first hour. It is ready when it fills the tray and looks puffy and bubbly.

steps.title: Prepare the toppings
steps.text: Drain the tomatoes in the sieve for 10 minutes, discard the juice and blend with the oil, oregano and salt. Toss the potato slices with the oil, rosemary, salt and pepper. Thinly sliced potatoes cook through in the same time as the dough and crisp at the edges.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Put a shelf in the lowest position and heat the oven to 250°C (fan 230°C), or its maximum, for at least 30 minutes. Bottom heat crisps the oiled base of the tray.

steps.title: Dimple and top
steps.text: Dimple the dough all over with oiled fingertips. Spread the tomato over one half along the long side, and lay the potatoes over the other half in overlapping rows, then sprinkle the Parmesan over the potatoes and drizzle the last 1 tbsp oil over everything. Dimpling knocks out the biggest air pockets so the toppings sit evenly.

steps.title: Bake and add mozzarella
steps.text: Bake for 20-25 minutes, until the base is evenly browned and crisp, the potato edges are golden and the tomato half is bubbling. Scatter the mozzarella over the tomato half and bake for 5 minutes more, until just melted. Adding fresh mozzarella late stops it releasing water and turning rubbery.

steps.title: Rest and cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, loosen with the spatula and slide onto the board. Scatter the basil over the tomato half and cut into 12 rectangles, 6 of each topping.

tips: A common mistake is adding extra flour because the dough feels too wet; keep your hands wet instead, as that moisture creates the airy crumb.
Slice the potatoes evenly at 2mm, or thicker pieces will stay firm while the thin ones burn.
Do not force the cold dough into the corners straight away; let it relax and it will spread easily.
Pat the mozzarella dry before adding it so it melts without making the topping watery.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot oven or a dry frying pan until piping hot (74°C).
